title: hardware-profiled kernel allocator and KV-warmup pipeline refactor for mixed-sku MIG nodes
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: On mixed-sku clusters (H100 / L40S / A10) with MIG partitions enabled, we observe elevated tail latencies during the initial KV cache population and first decode steps. Root causes include suboptimal kernel choice for short-sequence initializations, clock governor hysteresis on dynamic-frequency boards, and contention from concurrent micro-batches that defeat our previous static batching heuristics. Goals: reduce 95th/99th percentile latency for cold requests by 20-35%, keep aggregate throughput within +/-5% of baseline, and avoid regressions for long-sequence workloads. Proposed solution: 1) Implement a hardware-profiled kernel allocator that selects microkernels using a short-telemetry fingerprint collected at request admission (GPU SKU, MIG slice size, available clock headroom, per-slice occupancy). The allocator prefers lowlatency small-sequence kernels for KV-warmup and then seamlessly upgrades to high-throughput kernels for decode. 2) Refactor the KV-warmup pipeline to run a lightweight, non-blocking warmup pass (KV-warmup lanes) that uses a bounded number of tokens to prime caches without reserving full execution slots. 3) Add a frequency-hysteresis-aware clock hint to the runtime so the scheduler avoids triggering aggressive clock boosts for bursty warmup work on H100 L40S boards; instead it prefers packing warmups into existing high-frequency windows. 4) Introduce a MIG slice occupancy estimator that accounts for partition-level memory pressure and affinity, enabling kernel allocator to avoid destructive packing on heavily utilized slices. Implementation plan: - Phase A (this sprint): design + internal perf harness, telemetry schema, small in-process prototype of kernel allocator that works as a pluggable component. - Phase B: KV-warmup pipeline refactor + micro-batching lanes, end-to-end perf tests on h100-l40s+a10 mixed pool. - Phase C: rollout as opt-in feature behind runtime flag; run canary on dedicated capacity; gather telemetry and iterate. Benchmarks & targets: local perf harness (harness-ml1) shows initial warmup 95p 420ms -> target 280ms (~33% improvement). End-to-end canary expected to validate 20-35% 95p improvement under realistic traffic. Trade-offs & risks: - Risk of increased engineering complexity in allocator; mitigate via heavily tested pluggable interface and feature flag. - Some workloads may see slightly higher 50p due to packing decisions; will monitor metrics and provide per-route override. - Clock-hinting relies on conservative heuristics to avoid power/thermal regressions; tie to telemetry for safe rollbacks. Observability & rollout: add two new runtime metrics: kernel_alloc_path (enum) and kv_warmup_tokens (int), plus per-slice clock_hint events. Dashboards: perf/runtime/kv-warmup and perf/runtime/kernel-allocator. Rollout plan: opt-in flag -> internal canary on staging -> 2% production -> 10% -> 100% after 4 weeks if SLOs stable.
